entries.title: Jeremiah 9:2
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: A lodging place - Some retiring place, though it were but some mean hut in the wilderness.

entries.title: Jeremiah 9:5
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Weary - They use industry, and contrivance in it, they spare no labour.

entries.title: Jeremiah 9:7
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Try them - By melting them, I will bring upon them, the fire of the Chaldean war, that shall purge away those deceits in which they trust, that the remnant may be purified. For how - I have tried all other means.

entries.title: Jeremiah 9:10
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Wailing - The prophet having taken up a lamentation for the slaughter of the people, now re - assumes it for the desolation of the whole land. The mountains shall not be able to secure them, nor the valleys to feed them.

entries.title: Jeremiah 9:12
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Who is - Is there not a wise man among you, that will search into the cause of all these threatened judgments.

entries.title: Jeremiah 9:16
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: A sword - But I will follow them with the sword, 'till they be destroyed, such of them as were appointed for destruction; for otherwise, they were not all consumed, a full end was not to be made.

entries.title: Jeremiah 9:17
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Women - Who were hired to tear their hair, and beat their breasts, with other mourning postures, a foolish custom which has obtained in most ages and countries. Cunning - Such as are most skilful in it.

entries.title: Jeremiah 9:20
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Every one - It denotes how large and universal the mourning shall be.

entries.title: Jeremiah 9:21
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Death - The unavoidableness of the ruin is expressed metaphorically, alluding to the storming of a city, wherein there is no respect had to sex, youth, or age.

entries.title: Jeremiah 9:22
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: As the handful - They shall be no more regarded than a few scattered ears that drop out of the reapers hand, which either lie on the ground and are eaten by birds, or trod to dirt by beasts. None - None shall have so much respect to them, as to afford burial.

entries.title: Jeremiah 9:24
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Knoweth - Whether we make any curious distinction between understanding God, as if that be more speculative, whereby we rightly apprehend his nature; and knowing God, as if that be more practical, as directing the conversation, we need not here enquire; yet certainly both center in this, that we so know and understand God as to trust in him, and depend on him alone in all conditions. Exercise - Kindness, as it relates to his own people; judgment, in punishing the wicked; righteousness, as he deals justly and uprightly with both.
